analysis.title: South Korea Tech: Memory Pricing Tracker: Oct. 2026: 4Q26 DRAM ASP forecast for PC higher, server/mobile in-line, NAND lower than GSe
key_insights: TrendForce expects 4Q26 DRAM ASP for PC/server/mobile to rise +13-18%/+10-15%/+0-5% qoq, and eMMC/UFS ASP to rise +4-9% qoq. Versus GS estimates, PC DRAM is higher, server and mobile DRAM are broadly in line, and eMMC/UFS NAND is lower.

PC DRAM: October ASP of 8GB DDR4 modules rose 15% to $170 and 8GB DDR5 modules reached $165, so the DDR5 discount to DDR4 narrowed to 3% from 10% in September. TrendForce's +13-18% qoq 4Q26 forecast is above GS estimates for SEC/Hynix of +8-13%.

TrendForce says several PC OEMs have revised down 4Q26 and 2027 procurement plans. It also expects South Korean suppliers to cut PC DRAM output by more than 20% yoy in 2027 as capacity shifts toward server memory.
Server DRAM: October 64GB DDR4 and DDR5 module prices rose 15% and 11% to $1,490 and $1,685. The DDR5 premium over DDR4 fell to 13% from 17% in September.
TrendForce keeps its 4Q26 server DRAM forecast at +10-15% qoq, in line with GS's SEC/Hynix average server DRAM price growth estimate of 11% qoq.

TrendForce raised its 2026 server shipment growth forecast from +17.0% to +19.7%, citing stronger compute requirements from emerging US cloud service providers such as xAI, and slightly raised 2027 server shipments.

Mobile DRAM: TrendForce maintains 4Q26 pricing growth of +0-5% qoq, in line with GS's +3% qoq estimate for SEC/Hynix. Momentum is slowing because smartphone brands built inventory aggressively over the past three quarters and lowered full-year production targets.

eMMC/UFS: TrendForce expects 4Q26 TLC eMMC and UFS prices to rise +4-9% and +5-7% qoq, below GS's NAND ASP growth estimates of +7-10% for SEC/Hynix. It cites elevated inventories, rising costs and buyer resistance, with procurement shifting to Chinese suppliers offering smaller price hikes.
TrendForce expects NAND pricing momentum to slow further in 1Q27 amid weak consumer demand, inventory digestion and incremental NAND capacity additions.
GS reiterates Buy ratings on Samsung Electronics (on its Conviction List) and SK Hynix.
Exhibit 1 shows DDR5 16Gb spot trading at a 23% premium to the latest contract price. Exhibit 2 shows DDR4 8Gb spot at a 38% premium to contract.

market_movers.rationale: Buy on common and preferred shares, with the common shares on the Conviction List. The 12m target price is an EV/EBITDA-based SOTP on 2026E-2027E. The preferred target applies a 24% discount to common. Samsung Electronics has no US listing, so the ticker is left empty.
The 12m target price is based on 2026E/27E average P/E at a 7.0x target multiple. SK Hynix has no US listing, so the ticker is left empty.

sector_views.rationale: Contract prices keep rising across DRAM and NAND in 4Q26, with PC DRAM forecasts above GS estimates. Server demand is supported by higher shipment forecasts from US cloud providers. Mobile and NAND pricing is slowing.

earnings_insights: No earnings results are reported. GS estimates for SEC/Hynix 4Q26 pricing are: PC DRAM +8-13% qoq, server DRAM average +11% qoq, mobile DRAM +3% qoq, NAND ASP +7-10% qoq. These are GS forecasts, not reported figures.
risk_factors: Samsung key downside risks: major deterioration in memory supply/demand, sharp contraction in smartphone margins, and mobile OLED market share loss.

SK Hynix key risks: major deterioration in memory supply/demand and delayed technology migration, weaker smartphone/PC/server demand, Samsung's HBM progress affecting HBM revenue and profit, and lower AI-related capex reducing HBM demand.
PC OEMs have revised down their 4Q26 and 2027 procurement plans.
Smartphone brands built inventory over three quarters and cut full-year production targets, which reduces their willingness to buy more.
NAND buyers are resisting price increases, with procurement shifting toward Chinese suppliers.
